chunks: Then, your selection of them should not be based on your insight (firasah), your confidence, and your good impression of them,

for people expose themselves to the insight of the rulers through their affectation and good service, and there is nothing behind that (i.e., behind the good impression) of sincere advice and trustworthiness.
But rather, test them by what they did when appointed under the virtuous ones before you,
so choose the one who has the best reputation among the common people, and the most well-known for trustworthiness;
for that is a sign of your sincere advice to Allah and to the one on whose behalf you have been appointed (your Imam).

key_terms.تَصَنُّع: Affectation or feigned behavior to impress
key_terms.فِرَاسَة: Insight or intuitive discernment of character

ai.seo_question: How should a ruler select and verify the trustworthiness of his officials according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against the superficiality of *firasa* (personal insight), noting that officials often manipulate leaders through affectation and service rather than genuine integrity. He prescribes a rigorous empirical test: evaluating candidates based on their proven track record under previous virtuous leaders, prioritizing those whose trustworthiness (*amanah*) is visibly established among the general public. This method ensures that selection is rooted in objective merit and public verification rather than the ruler's subjective bias.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Your selection of these people should not be on the basis of your understanding (of them), confidence and your good impression,
because people catch the ideas of the officers through affectation and personal service and there is nothing in it which is like well-wishing or trustfulness.
You should rather test them by what they did under the virtuous people before you.
Take a decision in favour of one who has a good name among the common people and is the most renowned in trustworthiness,
because this will be a proof of your regard for Allāh and for him on whose behalf you have been appointed to this position (namely your Imām).
